tips_en: Read the skills analysis paper (Paper 3) first—it provides a foundational, mechanistic understanding of when and why procedural skills succeed or fail for LLM-based agents, establishing a conceptual lens that makes the other two papers more interpretable. All three share a common thread around 'skills': FACET synthesizes executable terminal tasks with verifiers, Zetta evolves runtime critics and recovery skills for embodied agents, and the third paper's finding that skills function mainly as procedural anchors (65.7%) rather than knowledge injection (4.5%) offers a unifying perspective on why both FACET's high verifier density and Zetta's validation-gated skill updates matter.
tips_zh: 建议先阅读第三篇论文——它从机理层面剖析了LLM智能体中程序性"技能"何时及为何有效或失效，提供了概念性视角，能帮助更好地理解另外两篇论文的核心设计。三篇论文都以"技能"为主线：FACET合成带验证器的可执行终端任务，Zetta通过在线演化运行时critic与恢复技能实现具身智能体的闭环控制，而第三篇的发现——技能主要作为"程序性锚点"（65.7%）而非知识注入（4.5%）——恰好为理解FACET高验证器密度和Zetta验证门控技能更新机制的必要性提供了统一解释。
